GitHub

28 integrations · three verification levels · one auth bar

Every tool behind one pasted token.

Each integration is its own command area, signs in with a long-lived token you generate once in the vendor's UI, and returns the same JSON envelope. Nothing needs a browser login at use time.

  1. unit

    Shipped, with its logic tested against stubbed HTTP. Never run against a real instance.

  2. live

    Run against a real instance; its common commands work there.

  3. stable

    In routine use against real instances, with its commands and output settled.

Dependency analysis

One command per source. You compose.

No single command quietly asks four services on your behalf. Build an inventory locally, then pipe it to exactly the sources you trust, and every finding says where it came from.

compose 
$ toil deps scan | toil osv vulns
$ toil deps scan > inventory.json
$ toil sonatypeiq evaluate --from inventory.json --application payments-api
CommandSourceCoversNetwork
toil deps scan Local manifests Package inventory for npm, Maven and NuGet None
toil deps diff Local manifests Packages added, removed or changed between two refs None
toil osv vulns OSV.dev Known vulnerabilities for an inventory Public API
toil ossindex vulns Sonatype OSS Index Known vulnerabilities for an inventory Public API
toil sonatypeiq evaluate Sonatype IQ Server Policy evaluation against an application Your server
toil deps frisk --source <one> The source you name Alias for the matching command above As above
toil deps outdated JFrog Artifactory Newer versions in your mirrors Your server
toil deps license-check JFrog Artifactory License metadata for an inventory Your server

Not planned

Some tools can't clear the bar.

If the only workable sign-in is a password, an interactive login, or another CLI, toil won't integrate it, however useful it would be.

  • ServiceNow

    Personal access tokens are opt-in and usually disabled, so in practice sign-in falls back to a username and password.

  • IBM UrbanCode Deploy

    There is no standalone personal token; the only workable sign-in is an account password.
